newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia reports sharply higher quarterly earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nokia reports sharply higher quarterly earnings.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications company Nokia Corp. said Monday its profits more than doubled in the second quarter, fuelled by robust growth in its mobile phone business.

Nokia, the world's leading manufacturer of digital mobile phones, said its profits more than doubled to 1.332 billion markka ($239 million) in the second quarter of 1997, vs. 518 million markka ($93 million) in the same period a year ago. The results came in just above the range forecast by analysts in a Reuters poll.

The company said net sales bounded to 13.06 billion markka ($2.35 billion) from 8.95 billion markka ($1.6 billion) a year ago. Mobile phone sales rose 49 percent, while sales of telecommunications infrastructure climbed 35 percent.
Despite the upbeat earnings report, some analysts said the company's stock may be due for a period of consolidation.
The results, coming after a stunning first-half profit increase from its Swedish rival Ericsson, were greeted by what what for Nokia was a relatively lukewarm stock response.
"Those were very good results," said Jyrki Hilli, analyst at Arctos Securities. "But after Ericsson, this was no knock-out surprise."
After closing at an all-time high in Helsinki on Monday, the company's American Depository Shares fell $1.875 to $84.875 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Richard Kramer, an analyst at Goldman Sachs in London, continued to recommend buying Nokia's stock, but said it may be wise to wait and see if the company can by deliver a new high-margin telephone handset to rival Ericsson's 788 and Motorola's StarTac models by year-end.

"Investors right now are looking for a new reason to buy Nokia and there's not really one in there (the report)," he said. "That said, there's certainly no reason to sell because of the trend in these results."
